sections.h2: Where Craven County deeds are recorded
sections.html:
The Craven County Register of Deeds is at 226 Pollock Street, New Bern, ZIP 28560. The phone number is 252-636-6617. The register is one of three county-wide elected offices created under North Carolina law.

Real estate work covers deeds, deeds of trust, plats, maps and any other instrument touching land. The same staff handle vital records, marriage licenses, assumed business names and military discharge records. Holdings reach back more than three centuries, so an old family tract can be traced through the same office that records a current sale.

For a seller, the practical rule is the cutoff. The office stops recording at 4:30 p.m. and does not swear in notaries after that time either. Ask your closing office how a late funding will be handled, since it would be filed the next business day.

An ordinary deed costs $26 for fifteen pages, and every page past that adds $4. A deed of trust is $64 for 35 pages, with the same $4 for each extra page.

The office takes cash, check or card for copies, vital records and marriage licenses, so call about any other payment type. Online vital-record orders through the county's vendor add a $3.50 convenience fee, which does not apply to a real estate recording.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax
sections.html:
The seller does. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the transferor pays the register before the deed is filed, at one dollar for every $500 of price or value.

  • Any fraction of $500 counts as a full $500 unit.
  • The money splits evenly between the county's general fund and the state.
  • The amount tracks the deed's stated consideration or value and shows on the seller's side of the settlement statement.

Your closing attorney will compute the exact dollars. The figure can differ from a simple price-based estimate if the price is not the full value of what changes hands.

The register's Real Estate page links three tools: an e-recording partner page, a public records search, and a page on UCC filings. A Recordation Notification page appears in the sidebar too, so ask the office what that service covers.

E-recording suits lenders and closing offices that send many documents. If an attorney handles your closing, you will rarely file anything yourself. UCC filings sent by mail take checks payable to Register of Deeds at the Pollock Street address.

  • Pull your vesting deed through the online search and check the legal description against it.
  • Look for a deed of trust with no matching satisfaction before you list.
  • For an inherited house, ask what the office holds under the wills and divorce decrees pages in its menu.

sections.h2: What registration does to your title
sections.html:
Registration fixes priority. Under G.S. 47-18, an unregistered deed, option, lease over three years or right of first refusal gets no protection against lien creditors and purchasers for value, and competing claims rank by time of registration.

That is why sellers ask for confirmation of recording after funding. A release of an old mortgage works the same way. Satisfactions cost nothing to record here, so confirm that a paid-off loan no longer shows as open on the index.

The contract for deed chapter, 47H, adds a recording duty of its own: the seller files the contract or a memorandum within five business days. A buyer may cancel during a three-business-day window, and forfeiture requires written notice with at least 30 days to cure. Anyone thinking of financing a buyer should read that chapter first.

sections.h2: Checklist before the deed is filed
sections.html:
A short review of the register's index and fee schedule before closing can catch problems that would otherwise surface after funding.

  • Confirm the index shows your vesting deed in the name you are selling under, with a legal description that matches the survey or tax record.
  • Check each deed of trust for a matching satisfaction. Satisfactions are recorded free, so a payoff lender has no fee reason to delay one.
  • Count the deed's pages. Anything over 15 pages adds $4 per page, and a deed of trust over 35 pages does the same.
  • Ask whether the instrument is non-standard, which carries a $25 fee, or whether several recordings are bundled in one document, which adds $10 for separate indexing.
  • Ask Tax Collection for the current-year payoff so the bill is not left open when ownership changes.

None of this replaces advice from your closing attorney, who sees the full title picture, but it gives you the questions to ask.

The county's planning department improved its Community Rating System class from 8 to 7, and owners in unincorporated areas now receive a 15% discount on flood insurance premiums, up from 10%. A buyer's insurance agent can confirm what applies to a given address.

Tax bills are separate from the register. They are due September 1 and carry no interest through January 5. Before closing, ask the Tax Collection Division at 252-636-6605 for a payoff figure so the bill is settled by the time the deed is filed.

If a home faces tax foreclosure, the county's foreclosure page lists properties for sale and gives the tax collection email for questions. Listed properties are not owned by the county, and owners are pointed to a state homeowner assistance site for delinquent tax help. If you would rather skip repairs and delays, our North Carolina page describes a cash sale.

Craven is a mid-sized, growing market. Population is about 105,025, up from 100,720 in 2020, in 50,334 housing units. Owners live in 68.4% of homes, valued at a median $231,600 for 2020 to 2024, and 553 building permits were issued in 2025. Eight towns, from Bridgeton to Vanceboro, sit inside the county, so ask the tax office whether a town levy applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: Where does a Craven County deed get filed?
faqs.a: In New Bern, at the register's Pollock Street office. Recording ends at 4:30 p.m., so ask your closing office how a later deed is handled.

faqs.q: What is the price of recording a Craven deed?
faqs.a: $26 for fifteen pages plus $4 per extra page. A deed of trust is $64 for 35 pages.

faqs.q: Does filing a mortgage satisfaction cost anything in Craven County?
faqs.a: No. A satisfaction of deed of trust is recorded at no charge.

faqs.q: Who covers excise tax on a Craven sale?
faqs.a: The seller. It goes to the register ahead of filing at $1 per $500 of consideration, with a partial $500 counted in full.

faqs.q: Can I look up Craven deeds from home?
faqs.a: Yes. The register links an online public records search, and its Real Estate page covers e-recording partners.
